title: Projection-normalized comparison of the integral completed coefficient presentations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and any scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $A^\uparrow$ denote the same ring raised to the small site's coefficient universe, with $d:A^\uparrow\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ the ring equivalence $x\mapsto x.\mathrm{down}$. Put $I=(\varpi.\mathrm{up})$, $P_n=A^\uparrow/I^n$ and $Q_n=(A/(\varpi^n))^\uparrow$ for $n\ge1$. On $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use the normalized finite coefficient presentations of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and the inverse-limit completed integral coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. There are unique ring isomorphisms
$$e_n:P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_n,\qquad e_n([x])=[x.\mathrm{down}].\mathrm{up},$$
and they commute with every quotient transition. Write $(P_n)_T$ for the finite coefficient ring sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], the sheafification of $U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and $(Q_n)_T$ for the constant ring sheaf of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The presheaf map sending an element of $P_n$ to the corresponding constant function induces, after sheafification, an isomorphism of ring sheaves $\kappa_n:\underline{P_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}(P_n)_T$, compatible with the quotient transitions. Put $\bar e_n=\underline{e_n}\circ\kappa_n^{-1}:(P_n)_T\xrightarrow{\sim}(Q_n)_T$. Let $B_T^{\mathrm{pbc}}=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and $B_T^{\mathrm{det}}=\varprojlim_n(Q_n)_T$, with projections $\pi_n^{\mathrm{pbc}}$ and $\pi_n^{\mathrm{det}}$. There is a unique ring-sheaf isomorphism $e_T:B_T^{\mathrm{pbc}}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_T^{\mathrm{det}}$ satisfying $\pi_n^{\mathrm{det}}e_T=\bar e_n\pi_n^{\mathrm{pbc}}$ for every $n\ge1$. Restriction along $e_T$ and its inverse are exact inverse equivalences on module sheaves [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Their unbounded derived equivalences [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] preserve cohomology bounds and identify derived finite reductions, their adjunction-unit maps, quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], and the associated product Roos diagrams $K\to\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nK_n$ of [def-weil-derived-complete] and [def-weil-derived-limit]. No constructibility or derived-completeness membership assertion is included.

proof.text: The lift equivalence sends $(\varpi.\mathrm{up})^n$ to $\varpi^n$, so $x-y\in I^n$ iff $x.\mathrm{down}-y.\mathrm{down}\in(\varpi^n)$. Therefore $[x]\mapsto[x.\mathrm{down}].\mathrm{up}$ is well defined; addition, multiplication and $1$ are preserved on representatives. The inverse sends $[a].\mathrm{up}$ to $[a.\mathrm{up}]$. These two formulas compose to the identity on every representative, and every quotient element has a representative, proving existence and uniqueness of $e_n$. If $b\geq a\geq1$, both composites from $P_b$ to $Q_a$ send $[x]$ to $[x.\mathrm{down}].\mathrm{up}$, with the last class taken modulo $\varpi^a$. This proves every transition square, including identities.

source.place: Section 6.5, coefficient convention; agent quotient-representative calculation, matching IntegralStratifiedPerfectCharacterization.lean lines 672–710

proof.text: The absolute value fixed in the coefficient datum restricts to the $\ell$-adic absolute value. Apply the integers-DVR theorem to this finite extension: $A$ is a DVR with finite residue field and $\varpi$ generates its maximal ideal. The valued-DVR finite-quotients theorem then gives finiteness of $A/(\varpi^n)$ for every positive $n$. Thus $Q_n$ and, by step 1, $P_n$ are finite commutative rings. Lifting changes neither their elements nor these finiteness properties.

source.place: Section 6.8, finite extension coefficient convention; valuation-ring and finite-quotient facts supplied by the cited existing nodes

proof.text: Fix $n$. For any object $U$ of the small pro-etale site, a continuous function $|U|\to P_n$ is constant on each connected component: a connected subset of a discrete space is a singleton. It therefore factors uniquely through $\pi_0(|U|)$; the factor is continuous by the quotient topology. Conversely precomposing a continuous function on $\pi_0(|U|)$ gives a continuous function on $|U|$. These inverse ring maps commute with restrictions and with postcomposition by every quotient ring map. The finite-constant-sections theorem identifies $\underline{P_n}(U)$ with these continuous functions, sending each constant-presheaf element to its constant function. Hence the functions presheaf is already isomorphic to $\underline{P_n}$; sheafifying gives exactly the specified $\kappa_n$, not an arbitrary isomorphism. The same postcomposition calculation proves that all $\kappa_n$ commute with transitions. Applying constant-sheaf functoriality to $e_n$ now gives $\bar e_n=\underline{e_n}\kappa_n^{-1}$ and its inverse, with $\bar e_aq^P_{b,a}=q^Q_{b,a}\bar e_b$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, discrete-space assertion, printed p. 30; quotient-topology factorization written out here for arbitrary U

proof.text: Use the sectionwise inverse-limit description. For each $U$, send a compatible family $(z_n)_n\in B_T^{\mathrm{pbc}}(U)$ to $(\bar e_n(z_n))_n$. It is compatible by the last identity in step 3. The inverse sends $(w_n)_n$ to $(\bar e_n^{-1}(w_n))_n$. These maps preserve ring operations and restrictions coordinatewise and their composites are identities. They define $e_T$ with the required projection equations. Any other map satisfying those equations has the same value in every coordinate on every section, hence is equal to $e_T$. Set $R=B_T^{\mathrm{pbc}}$, $S=B_T^{\mathrm{det}}$, $R_n=(P_n)_T$, $S_n=(Q_n)_T$, $e=e_T$ and $b_n=\bar e_n$ below. The normalization is $\pi_n^S e=b_n\pi_n^R$.

source.place: Tags 03CO (lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves) and 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits); coordinate calculation for the ring limits

proof.text: Apply ring-isomorphism tensor transport to $e:R\simeq S$ on the fixed small site: $C=\operatorname{Res}_e:\operatorname{Mod}(S)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is an additive exact equivalence with inverse $\operatorname{Res}_{e^{-1}}$. Indeed the two restrictions leave underlying abelian sheaves and maps unchanged, and the composite scalar actions are those through $e^{-1}e$ and $ee^{-1}$. Use the same result for each $b_n$ to obtain exact equivalences $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_{b_n}:\operatorname{Mod}(S_n)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R_n)$.

source.place: Tag 06YP (lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism), ring-isomorphism specialization; explicit scalar action as in the cited transport node

proof.text: The exact-functor derived theorem applies to $C$, $C^{-1}$, $C_n$ and $C_n^{-1}$. Their termwise extensions are triangulated on the unbounded derived categories. The ordinary inverse natural isomorphisms extend termwise and descend through localization, so the derived functors are inverse equivalences. Exactness identifies $C(\ker d/\operatorname{im}d)$ with $\ker C(d)/\operatorname{im}C(d)$, and thus $H^i(D(C)K)\simeq C(H^iK)$. An equivalence preserves and reflects the zero object, so every upper or lower cohomology bound, including any fixed interval, is preserved in both directions.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; inverse and cohomology calculation

proof.text:
Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to M$ over $S$. Ring-isomorphism tensor transport makes $C(P)$ flat-term K-flat over $R$. For every $n$ define the natural chain isomorphism
$$\alpha_n:C(P)\otimes_R R_n\longrightarrow C_n(P\otimes_S S_n),\qquad x\otimes a\longmapsto x\otimes b_n(a).$$
It is balanced because $\pi_n^S(e(r))=b_n(\pi_n^R(r))$; its inverse is $x\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes b_n^{-1}(z)$. Both composites fix pure tensors. These maps commute with restrictions and differentials and so induce maps on sheafified tensor complexes. They are natural in chain maps, since both orders send $x\otimes a$ to $f(x)\otimes b_n(a)$. Derived change of rings is computed by these K-flat models, giving
$$D(C)M\otimes_R^L R_n\simeq D(C_n)(M\otimes_S^L S_n).$$
The quasi-isomorphism and canonical resolution-comparison clauses of derived change of rings descend this natural chain isomorphism to the derived functors; consequently it is independent of the chosen resolution. No boundedness or flatness of $R\to R_n$ is used.

The normalized derived coefficient-adjunction theorem applies to $R\to R_n$ and $S\to S_n$, without a flatness assumption. On the flat-term K-flat models its unit is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Restriction of the target of $\alpha_n$ to $R$ is the same as first restricting along $S\to S_n$ and then along $e$, since the projection square commutes. Now $\alpha_n(x\otimes1)=x\otimes b_n(1)=x\otimes1$, so $\alpha_n$ intertwines these genuine adjunction units on K-flat objects. For arbitrary $M$, insert the inverse of $[P\to M]$ and use naturality to obtain the same equation. This identifies precisely the maps $c_n=[\gamma_n][P\to M]^{-1}$ in the integral reduction tower; it does not replace an adjunction unit by an unspecified map.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), identity-topos scalar extension; derived.tex Tags 0FND and 09T5; unit normalization on K-flat models

proof.text: For the adjacent transitions write $q_n:R_{n+1}\to R_n$ and $r_n:S_{n+1}\to S_n$. The coefficient identity is $b_nq_n=r_nb_{n+1}$. Applying $\alpha_n$ after $1\otimes q_n$ sends $x\otimes a$ to $x\otimes b_n(q_n(a))$, whereas applying $1\otimes r_n$ after $\alpha_{n+1}$ gives $x\otimes r_n(b_{n+1}(a))$; these coincide. For any $b\geq a$ the identical computation uses $b_aq_{b,a}=r_{b,a}b_b$. For iterated reduction, both orders of the balancing normalization send $(x\otimes a)\otimes a'$ to $x\otimes b_a(q_{b,a}(a)a')$. Thus the comparisons respect also the quotient normalization cocycle. All equations hold as maps of sheafified complexes before localization, hence in the derived categories. Together with step 8 they identify the entire inverse systems and their specified maps from $M$.

source.place: Section 6.5, finite quotient reductions; Proposition 3.5.1(1) and Definition 3.5.2, normalized quotient tower; explicit tensor formulas

proof.text: The countable-products-exact theorem applies to both commutative ring sheaves $R$ and $S$ on this small pro-etale site, for any scheme $T$. Therefore their module categories have exact countable products. Clause 2 of derived-limit existence supplies countable products in both unbounded derived categories, represented by termwise products. This verifies product existence for the reduction towers without assuming that $M$ is bounded, constructible or complete.

source.place: Propositions 3.1.9, 3.2.3(1) and 4.2.8, exact countable products; derived product consequence as in the cited existence node

proof.text: An equivalence $F=D(C)$ preserves these products: with inverse $G$, the bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(X,F(\prod M_n))\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(GX,\prod M_n)\simeq\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(GX,M_n)\simeq\prod_n\operatorname{Hom}(X,FM_n)$ exhibit $F(\prod M_n)$ as their product, with projections $F(\mathrm{pr}_n)$. Insert the level comparisons from steps 7–9. The first arrow of the Roos diagram has components $c_n$, which agree by step 8. The second arrow has nth component $\mathrm{pr}_n-t_n\mathrm{pr}_{n+1}$. Additivity of $F$ and the transition identity of step 9 identify this component with the corresponding one for the transported tower. Product uniqueness makes both squares commute. Applying the inverse equivalence gives the converse identification. This proves compatibility of the stated product Roos diagrams, without asserting that either diagram extends to a distinguished triangle or asserting any completeness membership.

tool_uses.why: The coefficient valuation ring is a DVR with finite residue field; generic coefficient arithmetic, not a replacement for proper base change.
Finiteness of each positive quotient is needed for the finite-constant-sections theorem; the unit contains no separate coefficient-arithmetic result.
Its normalized section isomorphisms identify constant and continuous-function finite coefficient sheaves on arbitrary schemes.
Exact scalar equivalence and preservation of flat and K-flat complexes for an arbitrary ring-sheaf isomorphism.
Termwise descent of exact scalar equivalences to unbounded derived categories.
Existence of flat-term K-flat resolutions for the arbitrary unbounded module complex.
Computation and canonical resolution independence of finite derived reductions, for possibly nonflat quotient maps.
The genuine unbounded scalar adjunction has the unit x mapped to x tensor 1 on a flat-term K-flat model.
Exact countable products for module sheaves over either completed ring on an arbitrary small pro-etale site.
